---
title: "Discussion Guide"
---

This page collects scientific and operational questions for group discussion during SHARK-Seq. It is not a quiz; it is intended to make workshop decisions explicit and reproducible.

## Reference DNA PCR

- Which MiFish forward-primer variant was selected for Reference PCR A, and why?
- What annealing temperature was calculated with the official NEB Tm Calculator?
- Was a common-temperature trial, gradient PCR or primer-specific program used?
- Which reference species / sample IDs were amplified?
- Are mitochondrial reference sequences or GenBank accessions available for in-silico amplicon-length prediction?

## eDNA PCR

- Which of the MarVer3, miniSharkR2 and miniSharkR5 assays were included in the actual workshop run?
- Were the calculated starting temperatures retained or changed after experimental observation?
- How were negative and positive controls interpreted?

## Gel electrophoresis and PCR clean-up

- Was one gel condition suitable for both short and long products, or were different gels used?
- Which bead ratio was selected, and is it appropriate for retaining the desired fragment-size range?
- At which point were samples pooled, if at all?

## Quantification and library input

- Which fluorometer and calibration were used?
- Which representative fragment length was used for each fmol calculation?
- What end-prep input amount was selected within the planned 100-200 fmol range?

## Flongle / MinKNOW

- Which Oxford Nanopore kit and Flongle version were actually supplied?
- Were any loading volumes changed after checking the current manufacturer protocol?
- Which MinKNOW version and basecalling model were used?

## Sequence analysis

- How were reads assigned to samples / primer systems?
- Was ONTbarcoder appropriate for each dataset type?
- Which expected amplicon length or length range was used in the analysis?
- Which database and criteria were used for sequence identification?
- How were reference-library sequences linked to environmental sequences?

## Record changes for the next protocol version

Use the repository discussions for methodological changes that should be considered for the next workshop release.
